papers.title: The Two-Level Poset Game is PSPACE-Complete
papers.abstract: Poset games form a fundamental class of combinatorial games that includes classical games such as Nim and Chomp. Determining the outcome of a poset game is known to be PSPACE-complete even for posets of height at most three. However, the exact computational complexity of Two-Level Poset Game, played on posets of height at most two, has remained an open problem for over a decade. We resolve this problem by proving that Two-Level Poset Game is PSPACE-complete via a polynomial-time reduction from Avoid True on positive CNF formulas.

papers.title: Towards Learning-Guided Discovery of Extremal Geometric Constructions: A PatternBoost Study
papers.abstract: Extremal constructions play a central role in the design and analysis of algorithms. Integrality-gap instances expose the limitations of relaxations, while hard configurations reveal structural sources of computational difficulty. Such constructions, however, are still typically discovered through a slow, manual process. This paper investigates how machine learning can accelerate their discovery to support algorithm design and analysis. We build on PatternBoost, a framework alternating local search with generation from a trained transformer, using its Axplorer implementation to investigate three problems: integrality gaps for maximum independent set of rectangles, integrality gaps for stabbing unit squares with axis-parallel lines, and hard instances for recursive guillotine cutting. By exploring candidate representations, local search operations, and surrogate models used to rank candidates before exact verification, we carefully adapt the framework to these combinatorial geometry problems.While naive representations and search strategies fail to find non-trivial instances, our tailored adaptation discovers numerous non-trivial constructions. For stabbing unit squares, the method reaches a gap of $20/13\approx 1.54$, improving on the literature's best known lower bound of $3/2$. Purely automated search converges rapidly and then plateaus, prompting the question of what is required to push the bound higher still. We find that initial instance diversity plays an important role: with modest expert input via a structured staircase construction, the system reaches an improved integrality gap of $14/9\approx 1.555$. These results demonstrate that machine learning and domain expertise can be combined to discover new extremal constructions that advance algorithmic lower bounds.

papers.title: Formalizing Flag Algebras in Lean
papers.abstract: Razborov's flag algebra method is one of the most successful tools for proving asymptotic density inequalities in extremal graph theory. It reduces an inequality about all large graphs avoiding a forbidden pattern to finitely many algebraic conditions, and a certificate satisfying them can be found by semidefinite programming. We formalize the method for finite simple graphs in Lean 4, building on Mathlib. The formalization covers flags and their densities, the flag algebra as a quotient vector space, positive homomorphisms as limits of graph sequences, Razborov's random extensions, and the downward operator that averages out labels. On top of this theory, we build verified computation of flag densities and a tactic that turns certificates found by semidefinite programming into Lean proofs. The certificate serves only as candidate data; Lean checks every fact the proof uses. With this development we verify seven Tur\'an-type upper bounds. Adding lower-bound constructions proved in Lean yields the asymptotic form of Mantel's theorem and the asymptotic Erd\H{o}s pentagon theorem $\pi(C_5;K_3)=24/625$; to our knowledge, the latter has not previously been formalized in a proof assistant. We also prove two inequalities of Goodman. All density theorems reported here depend only on the standard axioms of Lean's logic. Formalization also led us to treat forbidden subgraphs with a different semantics. Instead of building a separate flag algebra for each forbidden family, we keep a single algebra of all graphs and impose the constraint only when interpreting an inequality, through randomly labeled limits of graphs satisfying it. We prove that this ensemble semantics yields the intended density bounds, and that a condition we call root-plantability characterizes when it agrees with the standard semantics.

papers.title: Claw-Free and Line Graph Edge Deletion on Block Graphs
papers.abstract: Edge deletion problems ask for the fewest edges whose deletion gives a graph with a specified property. We study two such problems on block graphs. First making the graph claw-free, and second making it a line graph. Since every line graph is claw-free, the second problem is at least as difficult as the first. We show that on block graphs the two optimum values are always equal, and both are attained by the line graph of a forest. The main step is a completion argument, in which starting from any claw-free solution, we put back edges to get some nice structure inside each block still maintaining the claw-free property. This reduces both edge-deletion problems to the same problem of selecting vertices within the blocks of the input graph. We solve it by dynamic programming in $O(n+m)$ time, which also produces an optimal deletion set and a forest whose line graph is what remains after the completion argument. We also extend the method to $K_{1,r+1}$-free edge deletion for every fixed $r$.

papers.title: Edgewise Envelopes Between Balanced Forman and Ollivier-Ricci Curvature
papers.abstract: Evaluating Ollivier-Ricci (OR) curvature on large-scale graphs is computationally prohibitive due to the necessity of solving an optimal transport problem for every edge. We bypass this bottleneck by deriving explicit, two-sided, piecewise-affine transfer moduli between the transport-based OR curvature and the combinatorial Balanced Forman (BF) curvature. We establish deterministic bounds for $\mathfrak{c}_{\rm OR}(i,j)$ parameterized by 2-hop local graph combinatorics, reducing the edgewise evaluation complexity from an optimal transport linear program to a worst-case $\mathcal{O}\left(\max_{v \in V} \operatorname{deg}(v)^{2.5}\right)$ time, entirely eliminating the reliance on global solvers. Empirical scalability benchmarks confirm these theoretical guarantees, demonstrating that the proposed transfer moduli yield significant asymptotic and constant-factor speedups over the steep polynomial scaling of exact OR evaluation. Furthermore, the tightness of these bounds is validated via distributional analyses on canonical random graphs and empirical networks, with the derived analytical bands enclosing the empirical distributions independent of degree heterogeneity, geometry, or clustering, providing a scalable, computationally efficient framework for rigorous statistical network analysis.

papers.title: Finding non-bisimplicial and triad-free minimal separators
papers.abstract: A $u\hbox{-}v$ separator in $G$ is a set $S\subseteq V(G)\setminus\{u,v\}$ such that there is no $u\hbox{-}v$ path in $G\setminus S$. A minimal separator in $G$ is a set $S$ such that for some $u,v\in V(G)\setminus S$, $S$ is a $u\hbox{-}v$ separator in $G$ but no proper subset of $S$ is. A set $S$ is bisimplicial if it is the union of at most two cliques. Recognizing graphs in which every minimal separator is the union of at most $k$ cliques is polynomial-time solvable for $k=1$ and NP-hard for every fixed $k\geq 3$. We settle the remaining case $k=2$ by giving a polynomial-time algorithm to decide whether every minimal separator in a graph is bisimplicial. A set $S$ is triad-free if its independence number $\alpha(S)$ is at most two. Given a graph $G$ and two vertices $u,v$, the problem of finding a $u\hbox{-}v$ separator $S$ with $\alpha(S)\leq k$ had the same complexity gap: it was known to be polynomial-time solvable for $k=1$ and NP-hard for every fixed $k\geq 3$. We resolve the remaining case $k=2$ by giving a polynomial-time algorithm that finds a triad-free $u\hbox{-}v$ separator or determines that none exists.

papers.title: Nonlinear fixed-distance codes via real lifts of moment configurations
papers.abstract: Let $A_q(n,d)$ denote the largest size of a code of length $n$ and minimum Hamming distance $d$ over an alphabet of $q$ symbols. For fixed $q\ge2$ and $d\ge4$ we construct codes with redundancy $n-\log_q A_q(n,d)\le(d-3)\log_q n+O(\sqrt{\log n})$ for all large $n$. No algebraic structure is imposed on the alphabet, and the codes are not linear. For $d=4$ and $d=5$ the coefficient of $\log_q n$ matches the Hamming bound, so the redundancy is determined up to lower-order terms. At distance four the codes are provably better than every linear code: by the polynomial-method bound for cap sets, $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear codes with $q>2$ require a strictly larger coefficient in front of $\log_q n$. The construction imposes moment checksums over an auxiliary finite field, as BCH codes do, but one fewer than the distance would normally require. The affine-line theorem from prior work describes the dependencies left by these checks. We exclude them by placing the code positions inside a specially structured subset of the field, built from Behrend's sphere construction with the help of algebraic number theory.

papers.title: Potatoes and Onions
papers.abstract: The first major step in the theory of graph minors of Robertson and Seymour was the grid theorem, a fundamental duality result describing that any graph of sufficiently high treewidth must contain a large grid as a minor. Since this pioneering work, multiple grid theorems have been established in structural graph theory, linking various width parameters of combinatorial objects with the non-existence of grid-like obstructions. In particular, Kawarabayashi and Kreutzer [STOC'15] proved a variant of the grid theorem for directed graphs that links directed treewidth with the non-existence of topological minors of large cylindrical walls. On the other hand, to study immersions of undirected graphs $-$ another containment relation that focuses on edge-disjointness, rather than vertex-disjointness $-$ Wollan [JCTB'15] introduced a parameter, tree-cutwidth, and proved that it is dual to immersions of large walls. In this work, we present a version of Wollan's parameter for directed graphs, the directed tree-cutwidth. The main result is a grid theorem for directed tree-cutwidth, establishing that it is dual to directed immersions of large cylindrical walls.

papers.title: Sparse universal graphs for planarity
papers.abstract: We show that for every integer $n\geq 1$ there exists a graph $G_n$ with $(1+o(1))n$ vertices and $n^{1 + o(1)}$ edges such that every $n$-vertex planar graph is isomorphic to a subgraph of $G_n$. The best previous bound on the number of edges was $O(n^{3/2})$, proved by Babai, Chung, Erd\H{o}s, Graham, and Spencer in 1982. We then show that for every integer $n\geq 1$ there is a graph $U_n$ with $n^{1 + o(1)}$ vertices and edges that contains induced copies of every $n$-vertex planar graph. This significantly reduces the number of edges in a recent construction of the authors with Dujmovi\'c, Gavoille, and Micek.

papers.title: Exploring the unleaved tree of numerical semigroups up to a given genus
papers.abstract: We present a new algorithm for exploring or counting the numerical semigroups of a given genus that uses the unleaved version of the tree of numerical semigroups. In the unleaved tree there are no leaves rather than the ones at depth equal to the genus in consideration. For exploring the unleaved tree we present a new encoding system of a numerical semigroup given by the gcd of its left elements and its shrinking, that is, the semigroup generated by its left elements divided by their gcd. We show a method to determine the right generators and strong generators of a semigroup by means of the gcd and the shrinking encoding, as well as a method to encode a semigroup from the encoding of its parent or of its preceding sibling. With the new algorithm, we obtained $n_{76}=29028294421710227$ and $n_{77}=47008818196495180$.

papers.title: Spanning-Tree Maximization Forces Isoperimetry in the Square Lattice
papers.abstract: We determine which connected sets of $N$ vertices in the square lattice support the most spanning trees, using all lattice edges between the chosen vertices. Every maximizer minimizes the number of edges joining the set to the rest of the lattice. Its shape is a rectangle with at most two straight strips of vertices removed at opposite corners. For $N\ge18$, the maximizer is unique up to translation, rotation, and reflection: an explicitly determined rectangle with one possibly empty corner strip removed along its longer side. The proof combines comparisons of Laplacian determinants with geometric comparisons of corner deletions. For $N=n^2$, we prove a sharp stability inequality that bounds the symmetric difference from a translated $n\times n$ square in terms of the loss in logarithmic tree count. Thus, nearly optimal tree counts force the vertex set to be close to a square. We also derive an exact product formula and a recurrence for the number of spanning trees in rectangles with a single corner strip removed.

papers.title: Biclique decompositions from Welzl orders
papers.abstract: A biclique decomposition of a graph is a partition of its edges into complete bipartite subgraphs. We consider graphs whose vertices can be ordered such that the neighborhood of every vertex is the union of a sublinear number of intervals. We observe that these graphs admit compact representations in the form of biclique decompositions of small size. Here, the size of a decomposition is measured as the sum of the number of vertices of its bicliques. Combining this result with the existence of suitable vertex orderings for graphs of low neighborhood complexity, as proven by Welzl in 1988, we recover and extend several known results up to logarithmic factors. These results include upper bounds on the Zarankiewicz problem, matrix multiplication, quantum circuit complexity, and shortest path algorithms in "well-structured" instances.

papers.title: Locating a Seymour vertex in oriented graphs having minimum outdegree at most 7
papers.abstract: A vertex $v$ of an oriented graph $D$ is a Seymour vertex if the number of outneighbors of $v$ is less than or equal to the number of second outneighbors of $v$ (vertices at directed distance exactly $2$ from $v$). Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture claims that every oriented graph contains a Seymour vertex. We propose the following stronger conjecture (Conjecture 1.4): given any oriented graphs $D$, there exists a minimum outdegree vertex $s$, and a Seymour vertex $v^*$ such that the directed distance from $s$ to $v^*$ is at most $\lfloor\frac{\delta^+(D)}{3} \rfloor$, where $\delta^+(D)$ denotes the minimum outdegree of $D$. The main contribution of this article is to show that Conjecture 1.4 is true for all oriented graphs having minimum outdegree at most $7$. This, in particular, improves the results of Kaneko and Locke (2001) which (implicitly) proved Conjecture 1.4 for all oriented graphs having minimum outdegree at most $6$. In particular, this yields Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture for this class of oriented graphs. We also construct a family of digraphs attaining the proposed distance bound, showing that it cannot be improved in general. Finally, by adapting existing arguments, we show that if Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture is true then given any oriented graph $D$ and any vertex $v$, it is always possible to find a Seymour vertex $v^*$ such that the directed distance from $v$ to $v^*$ is at most the outdegree of $v$.

papers.title: Improved Bounds for the Bilu-Linial Conjecture via Spectral Recovery from Mixed Determinantal Polynomials
papers.abstract: Bilu and Linial conjectured that every finite $d$-regular graph with $d \geq 2$ admits an edge signing $\sigma$ whose signed adjacency matrix $A_\sigma$ has spectral radius at most $2\sqrt{d-1}$. We prove that every signing meeting the mixed-root condition $r_{A_\sigma}\leq\sqrt{2(d-1)}$ satisfies \[ \rho(A_\sigma) < \frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}\sqrt{d-1}, \] where $r_{A_\sigma}$ is the largest root of the mixed determinantal polynomial $\chi[A_\sigma,-A_\sigma]$. The interlacing theorem of Ravichandran and Srivastava guarantees a signing satisfying the mixed-root condition, so our result improves the coefficient $2\sqrt2$ in their two-sided spectral bound. In the proof, we construct a positive matrix-valued probability measure supported on the roots of $\chi[A_{\sigma},-A_{\sigma}]$. The second moment gives a simple matrix inequality $A_{\sigma}^2 + dI \preceq 4r_{A_\sigma}^2I$, which yields a preliminary coefficient $\sqrt{7}$. Estimates for the fourth moment use information about short walks to obtain the coefficient $(3+\sqrt{5})/2$. For triangle-free graphs, the coefficient improves to $\sqrt6$, and for graphs with girth at least five, it improves to $\sqrt{35/6}$. As a result of independent interest, we extend the construction to $\chi[A_1,\ldots,A_k]$ for Hermitian matrices $A_1,\ldots,A_k$ with zero diagonal, and compute the first two moments explicitly. Finally, an explicit signing of $K_8$ shows that the mixed-root condition alone cannot guarantee a coefficient below $(4+\sqrt5)/\sqrt6$.

papers.title: Stabilizer entropy cones as self-dual slices of linear rank cones: a five-party gap and dependence on the local dimension
papers.abstract: Entanglement entropies of multipartite pure states satisfy linear inequalities; for stabilizer states, the backbone of quantum error correction, the achievable entropy vectors generate a convex cone. We show that, after a linear lift, the closure of this cone is exactly the self-dual slice of a classical object on one more element than there are parties: the closed cone generated by the rank functions of arrangements of subspaces over $\mathrm{GF}(d)$ for a prime local dimension $d$, and of subgroups of abelian groups of exponent dividing $d$ in general. This correspondence brings two features of rank inequalities into play. First, the purifier acts as an extra variable: already for five parties the stabilizer cone is strictly smaller than the quantum linear rank cone, with which earlier evidence suggested it might coincide; an explicit six-variable inequality witnesses the gap. Second, the characteristic of the field enters, so the cone depends on the local dimension. It does not for up to four parties. With enough parties, the cone of $\mathbb{Z}_d$ qudits is contained in that of $\mathbb{Z}_{d'}$ qudits if and only if $d$ divides $d'$, and already for six parties the logical zero state of Steane's code lies outside the stabilizer cone of every odd local dimension. For this last result we show that the seven-variable characteristic-dependent inequalities we checked all follow from Shannon inequalities on the self-dual slice, and instead transfer one of them through a family of subgroups derived from the Fano plane.

papers.title: On composition and decomposition operations for vector spaces, graphs and matroids
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the ideas of composition and decomposition in the context of vector spaces, graphs and matroids. For vector spaces $\V_{AB},$ treated as collection of row vectors, with specified column set $A\uplus B,$ we define $\V_{SP}\lrarv \V_{PQ}, S\cap Q= \emptyset, $ to be the collection of all vectors $(f_S,f_Q)$ such that $(f_S,f_P)\in \V_{SP}, (f_P,f_Q)\in \V_{PQ}$. An analogous operation $\G_{SP}\lrarg \G_{PQ}\equivd \G_{PQ}$ can be defined in relation to graphs $\G_{SP}, \G_{PQ},$ on edge sets $S\uplus P, P\uplus Q,$ respectively in terms of an overlapping subgraph $\G_P$ which gets deleted in the right side graph (see for instance the notion of $k-sum$ \cite{oxley}). For matroids we define the `linking' $\M_{SP}\lrarm \M_{PQ} \equivd (\M_{SP}\vee \M_{PQ})\times (S\uplus Q)$, denoting the contraction operation by '$\times$'. In each case, we examine how to minimize the size of the `overlap' set $P,$ without affecting the right side entity. In the case of vector spaces, there is a polynomial time algorithm for achieving the minimum, which we present. Similar ideas work for graphs and for matroids under appropriate conditions. Next we consider the problem of decomposition. Here, in the case of vector spaces, the problem is to decompose $\V_{SQ}$ as $\V_{SP}\lrarv \V_{PQ},$ with minimum size $P.$ We give a polynomial time algorithm for this purpose. In the case of graphs and matroids we give a solution to this problem under certain restrictions.

papers.title: Maximum Likelihood Degrees via One-Edge Chordal Completion
papers.abstract: The maximum likelihood degree of a Gaussian graphical model measures the algebraic complexity of its likelihood equations. This paper studies maximum likelihood degrees of Gaussian graphical models through chordal completion. When a graph becomes chordal after one missing edge is added, its maximum likelihood degree is determined by the maximal cliques and clique-tree separators containing that edge. This recovers Uhler's formula for complete bipartite graphs with one part of size two, and extends it to deleted-spine clique books, whose degree is unchanged when a page is thickened to a clique. For several fill edges, the same method gives a product formula when no clique or separator bag contains two fill edges. We also determine four classes of vertices at which clique blow-up preserves the degree. Two follow from known results, and two are established here.

papers.title: Minimal Resolutions of $k$-divisible and $(k-1)$-dominant Ideals
papers.abstract: We introduce invariants we call $k$-divisibility and $d$-dominance, which are combinatorial constraints on the minimal generators of monomial ideals. We then prove that $k$ (respectively, $d$) is an upper bound (respectively, lower bound) for the projective dimension of a $k$-divisible (respectively, $d$-dominant) monomial ideal. This leads us to an explicit minimal resolution of $k$-divisible, $d$-dominant ideals when $d=k-1$ via a Lyubeznik resolution. This framework allows us to prove a conjecture made by Alesandroni. Using these invariants, we also provide a characterization of monomial ideals whose minimal free resolution is attainable from the Taylor resolution by performing exactly one consecutive cancellation. We also prove that for all $q,k,d$ in the range $1\leq d<k \leq q-1$, there exist monomial ideals that are $k$-divisible and $d$-dominant with $q$ minimal generators.

papers.title: The parity module of a matroid
papers.abstract: We introduce the parity module of a matroid with coefficients in a field $\mathbb{k}$. When $\mathbb{k}$ has characteristic zero, we show that the parity module of a matroid is isomorphic to its intersection cohomology module, yielding a new intrinsic characterization of the latter. The structure and dimension of the parity module can vary depending on the characteristic, giving rise to characteristic-dependent generalizations of the Kazhdan-Lusztig and Z-polynomials of matroids. When the matroid is realizable over the complex numbers, the parity module is isomorphic to the hypercohomology of the parity sheaf supported on the arrangement Schubert variety of any such realization. We also introduce the notion of pure modules over any field $\mathbb{k}$ and show that they satisfy a matroid analogue of the Beilinson-Bernstein-Deligne-Gabber decomposition theorem: Every pure module over the graded M\"obius algebra decomposes as a direct sum of shifts of the parity modules of matroids obtained by restricting to flats.

papers.title: Topological recursion for spin enumeration of hypermaps
papers.abstract: We establish topological recursion for the spin enumeration of hypermaps, or, in the dual language, spin dessins d'enfants. This problem has remarkable features distinguishing it from other applications of topological recursion to enumerative combinatorics. First, the spectral curve is elliptic rather than rational, as in most cases studied before. Second, it contains degenerate ramification points, and one has to apply a version of degenerate topological recursion. Finally, the meromorphic correlator differentials have "moving" poles on the antidiagonals between pairs of distinct arguments, and one has to adjust the loop equations to this kind of degeneracy as well. The computations involve concepts of different kinds, such as BKP integrability, Gaussian integrals, the x-y swap, and symplectic duality.

papers.title: Complete counterexamples to Mubayi's supersaturation conjecture for graphs
papers.abstract: For a graph $F$, its extremal number ${\rm ex}(n,F)$ and extremal graphs denote the maximum number of edges in $F$-free graphs and the graphs attaining this maximum, respectively. Let $h_F(n,q)$ be the minimum number of copies of $F$ in an $n$-vertex graph with ${\rm ex}(n,F)+q$ edges, and let $t_F(n,q)$ denote the corresponding minimum obtained by adding $q$ edges to an extremal graph. Mubayi (2013) conjectured that for every non-$r$-partite stable $r$-uniform hypergraph $F$ with $r\ge 2$, $h_F(n,q)\ge q\cdot t_F(n,1)$ holds for all sufficiently large $n$ and all integers $q\ge 1$. In this paper, we prove that Mubayi's conjecture fails in a stronger sense. For every integer $d\ge 2$, we construct a family of non-$d$-partite stable graphs $F$ such that $h_F(n,q)< q\cdot t_F(n,1)$ for all $1\le q\le O\bigl(n^{4/ 3}\bigr)$. In particular, these examplesis completely refute Mubayi's conjecture. \noindent\emph{Key words}: extremal graph; supersaturation; chromatic number.

papers.title: Uniform adjacency-degree probes from differential rigidity
papers.abstract: We construct a fixed triangular family of noncommutative polynomials that spans the joint cyclic module of a real symmetric pair from any prescribed vector. In dimension at most $N$, when the second matrix has spectral diameter at most $N-1$, the family has $N(N+1)/2$ members, degree at most $N-1$, and a shared arithmetic circuit of size $O(N^2)$. No rank-dependent choice of coefficients is made. The proof uses a rational differential connection with a small self-adjoint residue: a primitive polynomial exterior vector for an invariant subspace must have an integer degree smaller than one. For connected trees, the probes and the pointed adjacency--degree reconstruction theorem give one explicit self-adjoint polynomial $p_N\in\mathbb{Z}\langle a,d\rangle$ whose trace separates all trees of order at most $N$. Its circuit has $O(N^2)$ gates, formal degree at most $3N-2$, and polynomial bit complexity. Only the original adjacency and degree matrices, the identity, and ordinary matrix arithmetic are used. A separate integer sum-of-squares construction gives a fixed positive semidefinite representative on which the all-one vector is cyclic; its degree is $O(N^2)$. A linear trace-degree lower bound shows that the first construction has the correct asymptotic degree scale.

papers.title: Ordinary and measurable colorings of Euclidean three-space
papers.abstract: A proper coloring of Euclidean space is a coloring that assigns different colors to points at distance one. Using the planar character-law rigidity theorem of OpenAI, we prove that every finite proper coloring of $\R^3$ can be replaced by a proper Lebesgue-measurable coloring with the same number of colors. As a corollary we obtain that the ordinary and measurable chromatic numbers of $\R^3$ are equal, and both lie between $7$ and $15$.

papers.title: Improved Sidorenko bound for hypergraph Turan densities
papers.abstract: For every fixed integer $r\ge3$, we prove that the Tur\'an density of every $r$-uniform hypergraph $F$ with $m\ge1$ edges satisfies $\pi(F)\le1-c_rm^{-(r-1)/r}$, where $c_r>0$ depends only on $r$. This improves Sidorenko's general bound, whose gap from $1$ is of order $m^{-1}$. Complete $r$-uniform hypergraphs show that the exponent $(r-1)/r$ is optimal. The proof combines a potential argument for partial embeddings with the Lov\'asz Local Lemma.

papers.title: Internal partitions of $5$-regular and $8$-regular graphs
papers.abstract: An \emph{internal partition} of a graph is a partition of its vertex set into two nonempty parts such that every vertex has at least half of its neighbors in its own part. DeVos asked whether, for every fixed positive integer $r$, all but finitely many $r$-regular graphs admit an internal partition. This was previously known to hold only for $r\in\{3,4,6\}$. In this paper, we confirm this for $r\in\{5,8\}$ by proving that every $r$-regular graph on at least $10^7$ vertices has an internal partition.

papers.title: A combinatorial proof of the Chan--Robbins--Yuen volume formula
papers.abstract: The Chan--Robbins--Yuen polytope $\mathrm{CRY}_{m+1}$ has normalized volume $\prod_{j=1}^{m-1}C_j$, a product of Catalan numbers. Zeilberger proved the formula using the Morris constant-term identity; finding a combinatorial proof remained an open problem. We give such a proof by counting nonnegative integer flows. We add an extra edge from each vertex to a common sink and count flows according to how many of these edges carry positive flow. A double count proves a special case of a recurrence of Morales and Shi and gives these counts in terms of Narayana numbers. Deleting the first vertex then yields the Catalan product. We also give an explicit bijection for the recurrence and prove the corresponding reduction formula posed by Postnikov.

papers.title: Enumeration of one-cycle signed chord diagrams and their duals for optimal Morse flows on closed surfaces
papers.abstract: Optimal Morse vector fields on closed surfaces, i.e.\ fields with the minimal possible number of critical points (a single source and a single sink), are classified up to topological trajectory equivalence by one-cycle signed chord diagrams in Kybalko, Prishlyak and Shchurko (2018). We recall this construction and the associated duality, which corresponds to reversing the direction of the flow, in a unified encoding in which both endpoints of a chord carry the same label, and we make it algorithmic. We give an explicit traversal procedure that detects one-cycle diagrams, a canonical form of an equivalence class under cyclic shifts, reversal and relabeling of chords, and a construction of the dual diagram. On this basis we describe an algorithm that enumerates all one-cycle signed chord diagrams with a given number of chords, both for orientable and for non-orientable surfaces, groups them into equivalence classes, pairs each class with its dual, and identifies the self-dual ones. The algorithm is implemented in Python and archived in Zenodo; its output is validated against the Harer--Zagier numbers in the orientable case and against orbit-size counts in both cases. We also note that, when a one-cycle diagram is read as a cellular embedding of a one-vertex graph, its dual diagram describes the embedding of the dual graph.

papers.title: Graph binomial coefficients and a positivity conjecture of Guo and Krattenthaler
papers.abstract: We investigate Conjecture 7.4 of Guo and Krattenthaler \cite{GK}, which predicts that for every positive integer $n$, the polynomial \[ P_n(q) = \frac{(1-q)^2}{(1-q^{10n-1})(1-q^{15n-1})}\qbin{30n}{5n} \] has non-negative coefficients, except for $q^1$ and $q^{125n^2-25n+3}$, which equal $-1$. We study this problem through three main perspectives: First, by linking the boundary coefficients to the second differences of the partition function, we settle the first and last $25n+1$ coefficients via a novel partition injection. Second, by introducing a ``defect'' generalization of Andrews' classical lemma, we reduce the conjecture to an almost-unimodality property and employ a uniform saddle-point analysis to prove it analytically for all large $n \ge 2\cdot 10^{29}$. Finally, we connect these quotients to graph binomial coefficients, providing a natural orbit-counting interpretation via Burnside's lemma on directed cycles and paths.

papers.title: Bicolored Eulerian quasisymmetric functions, affine lengths, and Theta operators
papers.abstract: We introduce a $q$-analogue of the bicolored Eulerian quasisymmetric functions by incorporating an additional grading arising from affine length, obtained by interpreting bicolored permutations as affine permutations. We also provide an intrinsic description of this refinement in terms of bicolored permutations by introducing notions of alignments and crossings, together with an explicit bijection identifying these statistics with the alignments and crossings in the existing literature. Finally, we prove that our refinement is symmetric by expressing it in terms of the Theta operators appearing in the Theta coinvariant Conjecture and the modified Macdonald symmetric functions. Assuming the Theta coinvariant conjecture implies the Schur-positivity of our refinement.

papers.title: Reduction for flag-transitive symmetric 2-designs with gcd(k, {\lambda}) = p
papers.abstract: We study symmetric 2-(v, k, {\lambda}) designs admitting a flag-transitive point-primitive subgroup G of automorphisms, where gcd(k, {\lambda}) = p and p is a prime. In this paper, we show that G is of affine or almost simple type.
